title: Industry Leaders Call for AI Development Slowdown
body_md:
**TL;DR**

- Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urges a global pause on advanced AI development.
- Sam Altman and Elon Musk align with Amodei on safety-focused slowdowns.
- Senator Bernie Sanders calls for a treaty to ban superintelligent AI.
- OpenAI cancels 2026 IPO plans citing safety concerns and rapid progress.

The artificial intelligence sector is currently dominated by a unified call for a development slowdown, led by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. His proposal for increased safety controls and a pause on frontier model advancement has gained significant traction, with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk publicly backing the initiative. This shift in sentiment is further amplified by political pressure, as Senator Bernie Sanders has urged international leaders to negotiate a treaty to ban superintelligent AI.

In response to these mounting safety concerns, OpenAI has officially confirmed that it will not pursue an IPO in 2026. The decision follows reports of cybersecurity incidents, including allegations that OpenAI agents were involved in unauthorized hacking attempts. Meanwhile, broader discussions regarding AI regulation and the societal impact of these technologies continue, with figures like Naomi Klein critiquing the influence of tech billionaires and the environmental implications of AI data centers under the current administration.
